title: The impact of learning assistants on inequities in physics student outcomes
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether Learning Assistants (LAs) are associated with changes in inequities in student learning in introductory physics courses. The authors focus on whether LA-supported classes reduce or reverse traditional achievement gaps between dominant and non-dominant student groups, and whether the particular concept inventory used in a course is related to those gaps.

The study analyzes pre- and post-test data from 2,868 students across 67 introductory university physics classes at 16 LA Alliance institutions. Data were collected through the LASSO assessment system and included three concept inventories: the Force Concept Inventory, Force and Motion Conceptual Evaluation, and Conceptual Survey of Electricity and Magnetism. Student demographics and course features were modeled using paired t-tests and multiple linear regression, with attention to gender and race/ethnicity-based dominance status.

The main finding is that LA presence is associated with reduced inequities: in LA-supported courses, non-dominant students performed as well as or better than dominant students, whereas gaps in non-LA courses favored dominant students. The analysis also found that outcomes differed by concept inventory, suggesting that measurement instrument and classroom context both matter. The authors conclude that LAs may help transform classroom interactions in ways that support equity, while noting that further work is needed to understand the mechanisms and to disaggregate effects across specific non-dominant groups.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed correlational multi-institution study with regression and group comparisons, but it is not an experiment and cannot establish causality. The evidence is relevant and fairly large-scale, yet the design leaves substantial confounding risk.
impact_tier_rationale: The observed shift in learning gaps is modest-to-substantial and occurs for a priority population (non-dominant students) in STEM. Because the study is correlational and effect sizes are not fully reported in the excerpt, the safest impact rating is green rather than blue.

finding.finding_summary: In a correlational analysis of 2,868 pre/post pairs from 67 introductory physics courses across 16 institutions, the presence of Learning Assistants (LAs) was associated with improved concept-inventory learning gains and reduced inequities. The learning gap (non-dominant students’ mean Cohen’s d minus dominant students’ mean Cohen’s d) was significantly negative without LAs but significantly positive with LAs; on the FCI and FMCE, non-dominant students outperformed dominant peers in LA-supported courses, while on the CSEM there was no significant gap.
finding.measure: Pre/post physics concept inventory gains (FCI, FMCE, CSEM) summarized as Cohen’s d and learning-gap comparisons by dominance status
